Difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or getting restorative sleep, often affecting daytime energy and concentration.

A condition that weakens bones and increases the risk of fractures, often without noticeable symptoms until a bone breaks.
Sudden episodes of intense fear or discomfort that may cause palpitations, trembling, dizziness, and shortness of breath.

Inflammation of the sinuses that may cause facial pressure, nasal blockage, thick mucus, and reduced sense of smell.
Pain, scratchiness, or irritation in the throat, commonly caused by a viral infection but sometimes by bacteria or other irritants.
Soft-tissue injuries involving stretched or torn ligaments (sprains) or muscles and tendons (strains), often causing pain and swelling.
A Candida yeast infection that may cause itching, irritation, and discharge, depending on the part of the body affected.
Hearing ringing, buzzing, hissing, or other sounds when no external sound is present, sometimes associated with hearing changes.
Inflammation of the tonsils, usually due to infection, which can cause a painful throat, fever, and difficulty swallowing.
Pain in or around a tooth that may result from decay, infection, gum problems, or a cracked tooth.
A long-term inflammatory bowel disease affecting the large intestine, often causing bloody diarrhoea, urgency, and abdominal pain.
An infection of part of the urinary system that may cause burning when urinating, frequent urges to urinate, or lower abdominal pain.
Enlarged, twisted veins, usually in the legs, that can cause aching, heaviness, itching, or swelling.
A sensation that you or your surroundings are spinning or moving, often related to a problem in the inner ear.
Forceful emptying of stomach contents through the mouth, which can have many causes and may lead to dehydration.
Small skin growths caused by certain human papillomaviruses, often appearing on the hands or feet.
A highly contagious bacterial respiratory infection causing prolonged coughing fits, sometimes followed by a characteristic whoop.
Discomfort around a wisdom tooth, sometimes caused by eruption, trapped food, gum inflammation, or infection.
Parasitic worm infections that may affect the intestines and cause symptoms such as itching, abdominal discomfort, or digestive changes.
An overgrowth of yeast, commonly Candida, that may cause itching, redness, irritation, or discharge in affected areas.
A mosquito-borne viral illness that can cause fever, headache, and muscle pain, with severe cases involving jaundice or bleeding.
A bacterial intestinal infection, usually acquired from contaminated food, that can cause fever, diarrhoea, and abdominal pain.
